name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy has been actively releasing updates through mid-2026, with the latest being v2.28.0 (2026-08-27, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.28.0), a hardening release that caps cache replay sizes at 10 MB per topic, enforces new size limits on message titles (1 KB) and tags (512 bytes), and applies poll bandwidth to the visitor daily bandwidth limit. v2.27.0 (2026-08-04) dropped the 'experimental' label from PostgreSQL support, added email-based login, and hardened message templating against memory exhaustion. v2.26.x and v2.25.0 added security fixes for CPU DoS via templates, a ban-feed for abuse tracking, password reset via magic link, and web app improvements including configurable date/time formats.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL-2.0 (clients); check repository for exact terms
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026, most recently v2.28.0 on 2026-08-27
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — username/password auth, access tokens, email-based login and password reset, and per-topic access control
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud instance

breaking_excerpts: Message title is now limited to 1 KB and all tags combined to 512 bytes; requests exceeding these limits are rejected with HTTP 400 (error codes 40057/40058).
Cache replay is capped at 10 MB per topic per poll request; excess messages are truncated and an X-Messages-Truncated: 1 header is returned.
Message cache databases from ntfy older than v1.10.0 (November 2021) can no longer be migrated; upgrade via an older ntfy version first or delete the cache database.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a versatile open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server, so it lacks ntfy's built-in subscription model.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notifications and file sharing but is a closed-source commercial service with limited free tier and no self-hosting option, unlike ntfy.

alternatives.name: Ntopng / Alertmanager (Prometheus)
alternatives.review: Alertmanager excels at routing and deduplicating alerts in monitoring pipelines but is purpose-built for infrastructure alerting rather than general-purpose script-driven push notifications like ntfy.
